title: Rational and common-field point tensor descent
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, prime l!=p and algebraic closure Omega/Q_l. Given simultaneous integral point tensor comparisons I(E) [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-system], canonical integral witnesses C(E) [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-models] and their scalar squares [def-sf-point-integral-scalar-square], there are rational comparisons for the prescribed point functors and a common-stage comparison over Omega. They include the normalized module universe lift, exact derived fraction-field and field-scalar counits, rational tensor and unit models and scalar square [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-rational-compatibility], and every-common-stage tensor and base-stage unit formulas [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-common-stage]. These data are packaged in PointFieldTensorComparison. No finite or integral comparison is constructed by this conditional descent statement.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product (the finite-level geometric fibre case); at the integral, rational and common finite-field stages use the coefficient constructions of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], all integral constructible presentations allowed at the rational stage satisfy the integral finite-Tor hypothesis. Apply [lem-sf-tensor-comparison-localization-descent] to the integral comparisons just constructed, with their scalar squares. The prescribed rational and common-stage coefficient constructions therefore give the remaining comparisons, independent of representatives and with the required naturality, units, tensor constraints and coefficient squares. Use the prescribed coefficient/carrier lift, descend through its faithful finite-dimensional equivalence, and identify the exact derived scalar counits with mapDerivedCategoryFactors. The balanced chain tensor formulas determine the localization, field-scalar and common-stage tensorators. The common-stage equations do not mention finite-level data, so they hold after adjoining any finite family.

lean.statement:
theorem pointFieldTensorDescent
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Ω] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Ω]
    (I : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], PointIntegralTensorData D l hl E)
    (C : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], PointIntegralTensorCanonical D l hl E (I E))
    (hscalar : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L] (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L),
      PointIntegralTensorScalarSquare D l hl E L ι (I E) (I L) (C E) (C L)) :
    Nonempty (PointFieldTensorComparison D l hl Ω I)
